Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Pendleton OR
1004 PM PST Fri Nov 13 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...
- Active weather pattern through the weekend with mostly rain
  across the region, and light high mountain snow developing by
  Sunday

- Breezy to locally gusty southerly winds across portions of
  central and northeast OR will continue through the weekend

- A train of upper low pressure systems will bring progressively
  cooler conditions across the forecast area, with light to
  locally moderate mountain snow accumulations, and potentially
  a dusting in portions of central OR

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Water Vapor satellite imagery this afternoon shows
an upper level low offshore Vancouver Island the PacNW, while
visible satellite shows mostly cloudy conditions across the
PacNW, with areas of clearing around Grande Ronde valley and
Wallowa county. Meanwhile, radar shows embedded rain bands
starting to cross the Cascade crest, with light returns from
Yakima to the Redmond/Bend area. Southerly breezy winds have
developed throughout the morning across portions of central and
northeast OR as well, with some areas near the WA Blue mountain
foothills reporting gusts as well. 

Today through Saturday: The approaching upper low offshore the
PacNW has not only resulted in a strengthening pressure gradient
from central OR to the Blue mountains, but is also pushing a 
strong (45-65kts) 850-700mb jet streak east across central OR to
northeast OR. This has resulted in areas of breezy winds with
gusts 40-50 mph developing across these areas today, with winds
expected to continue into the evening hours.

Other than winds, the approaching upper low will push the band
of rain along the Cascade crest east through tonight, with 
light showers in the lower elevations and moderate to locally 
heavy showers across most mountain areas. 24-hr probabilities 
for 0.25 inches through Saturday morning are generally between 
50-85% across the eastern mountains and the Cascade crest/east 
slopes. As for most of the lower elevations (except the Lower
Columbia basin of WA), the probability of 0.1 inches is between
40-65%. Light Cascade mountain precip will continue into 
Saturday with dry conditions elsewhere while a transient ridge 
follows the exit of the upper low.


Sunday through Thursday: Next week is expected to start off 
with yet another upper level trough developing in the northeast 
Pacific that will push across the region through Tuesday. Ahead
of the low will be a cold/occluded frontal boundary that will
push a band of precipitation across the region throughout
Sunday, with the frontal boundary stalling across far eastern
OR/WA Sunday night into Monday morning. Monday, the upper trough
will drop into the PacNW, pushing whats left of the frontal
boundary into the northern Rockies, with precipitation mainly
limited to the Cascades, Blues, Elkhorn crest, and the high
terrain across Wallowa County. During the peak precipitation on
Sunday, snow levels will mainly be above 6kft in the mountains,
resulting in any snow accumulations being limited to the 
Cascade peaks, with a rain/snow mix down to around 5kft. Behind 
the frontal boundary, snow levels will drop to around 4kft, 
resulting in light snow developing along the Cascades throughout
Monday, with rain transitioning into snow along the eastern
mountains late Monday morning into the late afternoon. In
addition to lowering snow levels, temperatures will cooling
region-wide through Monday, with moderate-high 
confidence(55-75%) in afternoon high temperatures in the mid 
40s to low 50s.

Tuesday through Thursday, ensemble cluster members are in good
agreement that a transient ridge will slide into the PacNW
Tuesday with dry conditions, then yet another upper trough will
drop into the PacNW late Tuesday night into Thursday. There is 
increasing uncertainty in regards to timing/positioning of the 
trough late Wednesday into Thursday, but impacts amongst 
ensemble solutions remain similar during that period.

For Tuesday, while the ridge is overhead conditions will remain
dry, however temperatures will remain cool as a cold airmass
remains over the region. By late Tuesday night, the next round
of precipitation will arrive to the Cascades, then push east 
across the region as the trough pushes inland. There is moderate
confidence (50-60%) that snow levels will lower down to around 
2-3kft Tuesday night and Wednesday morning, then increasing to
around 3-3.5kft by Wednesday afternoon and evening. This will 
result in a light dusting (~0.1 inches) of snow in some lower 
elevation locations (confidence 35-50%) Wednesday morning, 
while there is moderate confidence (40-60%) in 3 to 4 inches of 
snow accumulations across the Cascades and eastern mountains
through Wednesday night. Late Wednesday into Thursday, forecast
confidence is low (15-20%) owing to positioning disagreements of
the upper trough as it continues to cross the PacNW. Solutions
from the ensemble cluster members range from light mountain snow
continuing, to light mountain snow and light low elevation rain,
to no precipitation during the Wednesday night to Thursday
period. Lawhorn/82

.AVIATION /06Z TAFS THROUGH 06Z SUNDAY/...

KDLS and KYKM shows LIFR to MVFR conditions overnight, with fog
present reporting lowest visibility of 1/2 mile. Fog conditions
expected to lift to MVFR - VFR by 10z(50% confidence). All 
other sites show VFR conditions, with wind gusts of 22kt for 
KBDN and KRDM for 18z onward. Overnight light rain showers for 
KPDT and KALW.
